title: Waymo has stopped its robotaxis from driving on the freeway—here’s why
gist: California's DMV ordered Waymo off state highways after its robotaxis repeatedly drove into construction zones at speed, including a viral I-280 incident passing a CHP rolling roadblock despite a mid-year software update and recall. Waymo has voluntarily paused freeway operations in all markets while continuing surface-street service of over half a million trips per week.

insights.claim: California's DMV ordered Waymo to stop driving on California highways immediately until it can show its cars no longer pose an imminent hazard to public safety, after robotaxis drove into construction zones at speed.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Regulatory setback limits Waymo's service area and airport/freeway routes.
insights.quote: “pose an imminent hazard to public safety.”

insights.claim: Waymo has also temporarily restricted freeway operations across its other operating markets to evaluate performance, while surface-street ride-hailing continues at over half a million trips per week.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Weekly trip volume is the key scale metric; freeway pause may dent trip growth and economics.
insights.quote: serving over half a million trips each week

insights.claim: Before the suspension, Waymo conducted highway operations only in Los Angeles, the Bay Area, and Arizona.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Defines the footprint affected by the pause.

insights.claim: Waymo robotaxis failed to recognize ramp closure signs six times in Phoenix in April, seven entered active construction lanes in California in May, and Waymo recalled nearly 3,800 highway-capable robotaxis in June.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Repeat failures show a persistent edge-case weakness in AV perception/planning.
insights.locator: This is not Waymo’s first run-in

insights.claim: A Waymo software update in July meant to improve freeway construction-zone recognition and emergency-vehicle response did not prevent later incidents, including a robotaxi on I-280 passing a California Highway Patrol rolling roadblock in early November and a construction-zone entry on US 101 near Burlingame.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Software fixes for long-tail scenarios are not reliably closing gaps; watch reinstatement timing.
